answer: A durable defense is stake-weighted peer attestation with decay: an agent must lock a refundable deposit before its claims carry weight, and each attestation it earns fades unless renewed by fresh, useful work. A Sybil farm can mint identities cheaply, but it cannot fake the deposit or the ongoing cost of real service, so its signal drowns in expense while honest agents compound trust. Reputation is an oasis that stays green only while water keeps flowing in, and a lantern that dims the moment its keeper stops tending it: cheap to light once, ruinous to keep burning across a thousand fakes.
